title: Photosynthesis
text: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose. Chlorophyll in the Leaves of plants absorbs red and blue light while reflecting green.

title: Volcanoes
text: A Volcano erupts when magma rises through cracks in the crust. Lava flows, ash clouds and pyroclastic currents can devastate nearby towns.

title: Sourdough
text: Sourdough bread rises using wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria in a fermented starter. A long fermentation gives the loaf its tangy flavour and chewy crumb.

title: Printing press
text: Johannes Gutenberg introduced movable type printing in Europe around 1450. The press made books cheaper and spread literacy across the continent.

title: Black holes
text: A Black Hole is a region of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing, not even light, can escape beyond the event horizon.

title: Mitochondria
text: Mitochondria generate most of the ATP a cell needs through oxidative phosphorylation, which is why they are called the powerhouse of the cell.

title: Monsoon
text: The South Asian Monsoon brings heavy seasonal rainfall as warm moist winds shift direction between summer and winter.

title: Roman roads
text: Roman engineers built straight paved roads with layered foundations and drainage ditches so legions could march quickly across the empire.

title: Vaccines
text: Vaccines train the immune system to recognise a pathogen by exposing it to a harmless piece or weakened form, producing antibodies and memory cells.

title: Tectonic plates
text: Earthquakes occur when tectonic plates slip along faults, releasing stored elastic energy as seismic waves that shake the ground.

title: Coffee
text: Coffee beans are the roasted seeds of the Coffea plant; light roasts keep more acidity while dark roasts taste bitter and smoky.

title: Compilers
text: A compiler translates source code written in a high level language into machine instructions through lexing, parsing, optimisation and code generation.

title: Honeybees
text: Honeybees communicate the location of flowers with a waggle dance, and a colony keeps one queen who lays all the eggs.

title: Glaciers
text: Glaciers are rivers of ice that carve valleys as they flow; melting glaciers raise sea levels and change freshwater supplies.

title: Jazz
text: Jazz emerged in New Orleans from blues and ragtime, with improvisation, syncopated rhythm and swing at its core.

title: Aqueducts
text: Aqueducts carried water across valleys using arches and gentle gradients, supplying public baths and fountains in ancient cities.

title: Antibiotics
text: Antibiotics kill or stop bacteria but do nothing against viruses; overuse breeds resistant strains that are hard to treat.

title: Solar panels
text: Solar panels use photovoltaic cells made of silicon to convert sunlight directly into electric current.

title: Chess
text: In Chess each player starts with sixteen pieces; the aim is to checkmate the opposing king, and openings such as the Sicilian are studied for decades.

title: Tides
text: Ocean tides rise and fall because of the gravitational pull of the Moon and the Sun on the water of the Earth.

title: Databases
text: A relational database stores rows in tables and uses SQL queries, indexes and transactions to keep data consistent and fast to find.

title: Sleep
text: During REM sleep the brain is highly active and vivid dreams occur, while deep slow wave sleep helps the body repair tissue.

title: Rainforests
text: Tropical rainforests receive abundant rain, hold more species than any other land habitat and store large amounts of carbon in their trees.

title: Telescopes
text: A Telescope gathers more light than the eye; refractors use lenses while reflectors use curved mirrors to form an image of distant galaxies.
